A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E are available and readable, allowing renamed methods and relocated material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic graph-recovery experiments, including comparisons and interaction ablations in Section 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original simulations and adds an evaluation on the Sachs biological-network dataset in Section 6.

M1.justification: BiNOTEARS combines the names of the existing DAGMA-HO small-graph implementation and NOTEARS-MLP-reg large-graph procedure. The interaction features, logistic objective, quasi-MCP penalty, acyclicity formulation, and two-stage refinement procedure were already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from exclusively simulated ER/SF graphs to include the Sachs protein and phospholipid network in human immune cells. This introduces the paper's first real biological domain while retaining the synthetic scenarios.

E2.justification: The new Sachs comparison evaluates linear NOTEARS and standalone NOTEARS-MLP against BiNOTEARS. v1 used NOTEARS-MLP within its proposed procedure but did not report this standalone comparison. Synthetic comparisons retain DAGMA, FGES, and PC; DAGMA-1st is simply renamed DAGMA.

E3.justification: The added Sachs evaluation uses 7,466 measurements of 11 variables and a consensus reference network, reporting edge counts alongside SHD. Existing synthetic sample sizes, graph configurations, pruning thresholds, and tuning values remain unchanged. Sachs preprocessing is not specified.

E4.justification: The interaction ablations in Figure 1(b) and the supplementary interaction-order comparisons in Figures 3–6 are retained. The Sachs table adds benchmark evidence without a new ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Figures 1 and 3 continue to specify standard-error bars over 10 replications. No changed run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported, and the Sachs table adds no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The synthetic curves in Figures 1–6 are unchanged after matching method names. The new Sachs table reports SHD/edge-count pairs of 22/18 for NOTEARS, 16/13 for NOTEARS-MLP, and 13/15 for BiNOTEARS. These are additional results, not improvements over corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: Main-text Equation (3) corrects the predictor factor from f_{p-1} to x_{p-1}. Lemma 1 also newly declares p_S in R^{|S|}, introducing a dimensional error relative to the 2^{|S|} configuration probabilities required by Definition 1. The substantive theorem statements and proof arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same general binary-model, nonidentifiability, sparsest-DAG, and Markov-equivalence claims. The introduction's explicit emphasis on sparsest recovery without faithfulness restates the existing unconditional part of Theorem 3 rather than extending its guarantee.

C2.justification: A new Section 6 footnote explains the solver choices through speed–accuracy tradeoffs. Conversely, v1's Section 4 footnote explaining the single observational environment and contrasting it with interventions or multiple environments is removed. The large-graph heuristic's lack of theoretical guarantees remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that DAGMA uses its original implementation's default parameters, but removes the Intel Broadwell/Skylake CPU, core-count, and memory specifications. The sigmoid adaptation, logistic loss, pruning thresholds, continuation settings, and implementation links were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Aragam (2024) as an exception involving nonparametric score-based search and Sachs et al. (2005) for the new dataset. It also sharpens the distinction from Deng et al. (2024), identifying the discrete parameter-to-adjacency construction as the missing connection.

P1.justification: The title adds 'and Causal Discovery,' method terminology is unified under BiNOTEARS, and selected introduction, related-work, and experimental paragraphs are edited. The topological-sort definition becomes a footnote, and implementation receives its own appendix subsection. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds an unnumbered Sachs results table and updates figure legends and captions to reflect method renaming. All six figures remain; appendix Figures 3 and 4 now share a page. These are limited display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves empirical breadth through the Sachs comparison and clarifies the existing implementations and research positioning. The benefit is limited by unspecified Sachs preprocessing, removed hardware information, and the new dimensional error in Lemma 1. The core method, synthetic evidence, and theoretical guarantees are otherwise unchanged.
